reality_delta: The dispatcher code now defines DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300 and DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 5. The run_provider_command loop catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired, records each attempt with timeout metadata, and reissues the command up to max_retries before raising ProviderTimeoutError. On final timeout, cmd_dispatch serializes all attempts to raw evidence and reports provider-timeout. The self-check uses a 0.2-second fixture with 1 retry to prove the retry mechanism works end-to-end. The prior 20260531 session manifest explicitly records that implementation follow-up provider reviews timed out without extractable structured review, marking the session main-decided with a documented Prism health risk — this is an accurate accountability boundary, not a retroactive claim of Prism acceptance. The enforcement-matrix and temporary_usable_check now require the provider-dispatcher probe.
main_concern: The self-check validates the retry logic via run_provider_command with a sub-second fixture, but it does not exercise the full cmd_dispatch path that writes timeout raw evidence to disk, nor does it verify that verify-evidence can parse a timeout-attempt raw file. The operational defaults (300s, 5 retries) are only verified as argparse constant values, not through execution. This creates a gap between "the retry mechanism works in principle" and "the complete timeout-to-raw-evidence pipeline works at operational scale."
top_risks: A regression in cmd_dispatch's raw evidence serialization on timeout would not be caught by the self-check, because the fixture calls run_provider_command directly, bypassing the raw-out writing path.
The self-check uses 0.2s timeout and 1 retry; a bug that only appears at higher retry counts (e.g., handle state corruption or argv rebuild failure across 5 retries) would not be detected.
